solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Have relations gone over a round hill?

indicators.note: something that has gone over has toppled and is upside down, so the word is turned back to front

parts.note: British slang for having sex

explanation.surface: A cheeky question about whether a couple have been making love up on a rounded hilltop.
explanation.walkthrough: BONK is British slang for sex; read backwards it gives KNOB, which also names a rounded hillock.
explanation.definitionFit: In British topography a knob is a small rounded hill or knoll, a sense found in place names.

clue.text: Fellow reversing around old lady in Rover

indicators.note: around tells us the turned word wraps itself about the old lady
reversing means the word for fellow is written backwards

parts.note: a don is a fellow of a university college
old lady is slang for mother, MA

explanation.surface: A man backs his car around his elderly mother in a Land Rover.
explanation.walkthrough: Rover looks like the car brand; it is a wanderer.
explanation.definitionFit: A nomad roams from place to place without settling, which is exactly what a rover does.

clue.text: Fish served up on platter is a bit off

indicators.note: in a down clue, served up means the fish's name is read from bottom to top

parts.note: a dab is a small flatfish
a platter is a large serving dish

explanation.surface: A fish brought to the table on a platter smells slightly suspect.
explanation.definitionFit: Something slightly bad or not quite fresh can be described as rather poor, a little off-colour, faintly spoiled.

clue.text: Western idol with accent needing improvement

indicators.note: work that needs improvement must be reworked, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A cowboy-film star whose drawl needs some coaching.
explanation.definitionFit: Occidental is the formal adjective for things belonging to the West, the opposite of oriental.

clue.text: Dutiful man giving support to old bishop

indicators.note: in a down clue, a piece that supports another sits beneath it, so it follows in the answer

parts.note: O is the standard abbreviation for old
B is the chess abbreviation for bishop
a manservant is a man, and to man is to serve

explanation.surface: A loyal attendant propping up an elderly bishop.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone observant keeps religious rules and customs carefully, so is dutiful in practice.

clue.text: Is it possible that son welcomes primate's nibbles?

indicators.note: to welcome someone is to take them in, so the primate goes inside

parts.note: can asks whether something is possible
S is the abbreviation for son
an ape is a primate

explanation.surface: Asking whether a boy will share snacks with his pet monkey.
explanation.definitionFit: Canapés are small savoury snacks served with drinks, so they are party nibbles.

clue.text: Dickens supported himself after retirement

indicators.note: retiring means withdrawing or going back, so the phrase is read in the opposite direction

parts.note: to live on something is to support yourself

explanation.surface: Charles Dickens kept himself going once he had retired.
explanation.walkthrough: Dickens looks like the novelist; in 'what the dickens' it is a polite word for the devil.
explanation.definitionFit: The dickens is an old euphemism for Satan, used in exclamations such as 'what the dickens'.

clue.text: Pampered clergyman tours boozer pointing heavenward

indicators.note: in a down clue, pointing heavenward means reading upwards, so the letters run backwards
to tour a place is to go all round it, so the clergyman surrounds the boozer

parts.note: a dean is a senior clergyman
boozer is British slang for a pub

explanation.surface: A spoilt vicar visiting a pub, with a nod to the heavens.
explanation.definitionFit: To nanny someone is to fuss over and coddle them, so a nannied person has been pampered.

clue.text: Drink in a romance novel set around island

indicators.note: set around means placed around something, so the rearranged letters enclose the island
novel means new, so the letters are given a fresh order

parts.note: taken as written
I is the abbreviation for island

explanation.surface: A coffee that features in a holiday love story on an island.
explanation.definitionFit: An americano is a coffee made by adding hot water to espresso, a drink sold in every cafe.

clue.text: A way in which ads are created abroad?

definitions.text: A way in which ads are created abroad?

parts.words: A way in which ads are created
parts.note: surface reading: a method of making advertisements

parts.words: A way in which ads are created abroad?
parts.note: setter's reading: a way is a street, and this one is the overseas home of the advertising business

explanation.walkthrough: Way sounds like method, but it means a road; abroad points to New York, where this avenue gave its name to the American advertising industry.
explanation.definitionFit: This Manhattan street is synonymous with the advertising agencies based there, so it is literally a road where adverts are made.

clue.text: Always covering key soldier makes you more anxious

indicators.note: covering means wrapping round, so the word for always encloses the rest

parts.note: e'er is a poetic contraction of ever
D is a musical key
a GI is an American soldier

explanation.surface: Constantly guarding a key soldier keeps you on edge.
explanation.definitionFit: Edgy means nervous or tense, and the comparative form describes someone more on edge than another.

clue.text: Glyceride discovered in Nepal! MIT investigates!

indicators.note: something discovered in a text is found sitting inside it, waiting to be uncovered

parts.note: the letters run across the end of Nepal, all of MIT and the start of investigates

explanation.surface: A news flash: a chemical turns up in Nepal and a famous American university is looking into it.
explanation.definitionFit: Palmitin is the glyceride of palmitic acid, a fat found in palm oil and many other natural fats.

clue.text: They are all I am, being great intellects

definitions.meaning: first meaning: conceited people whose every thought is 'I am', all about themselves
second meaning, read literally: large brains, or the people who have them

explanation.surface: Someone boasting that clever people are just like them.
explanation.definitionFit: Conceited show-offs are called this informally, and taken literally the word means people with large heads, a joking name for brainboxes.

clue.text: Ladies sit up for romantic types

indicators.note: up here means in disorder or upset, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Women sitting up to wait for dreamy suitors.
explanation.definitionFit: Idealists pursue perfection rather than practical reality, which is what romantics in the visionary sense do.

clue.text: Ring road by Ealing half closed off? Nightmare!

indicators.note: half closed off means the second half of the place name is shut away and dropped

parts.note: a ring is round like the letter O
RD is the abbreviation for road
Ealing is a district of west London

explanation.surface: A ring road near Ealing with half its lanes shut: a commuter's nightmare.
explanation.walkthrough: Ealing is a borough of west London; keeping only its first three letters gives EAL.
explanation.definitionFit: An ordeal is a painful, harrowing experience, which is what we loosely call a nightmare.

clue.text: Where one sees cat's eyes wandering about?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the highway, where reflective cat's eyes studs are set into the surface
second meaning: travelling from place to place

explanation.surface: Spotting a cat's glowing eyes while out roaming at night.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain cat's eyes are small reflectors set into the road surface, not a real cat's eyes.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase locates you on a highway, where those studs are, and idiomatically means travelling or touring constantly.

clue.text: Lady with pen that's been dropped in one's bitter

indicators.note: something dropped in a drink sits inside it, so the answer lies within the following words

parts.note: the letters run from inside one's into the start of bitter

explanation.surface: A woman's fountain pen has fallen into somebody's pint of bitter, a British beer.
explanation.walkthrough: Edith Nesbit wrote The Railway Children; bitter is a British pale ale.
explanation.definitionFit: Edith Nesbit was an English author of children's books, so she is a woman who wrote with a pen.

clue.text: Tipple linesman downs about lunchtime?

indicators.note: to down a drink is to swallow it, so the linesman takes the next piece inside

parts.note: a bard is a poet, someone who writes lines
CA is circa, Latin for about
one o'clock, written as the Roman numeral I, is lunchtime

explanation.surface: A football linesman having a drink around lunchtime.
explanation.walkthrough: Linesman looks like a match official; here it is a poet who writes lines.
explanation.definitionFit: Bacardi is a well-known brand of rum, a favourite alcoholic drink or tipple.

clue.text: Where one might go on lake in Battle

indicators.note: in an across clue, putting one piece on another means placing it after

parts.note: a lake is a body of water
loo is British slang for a toilet, where one goes

explanation.surface: Needing the toilet while out on a lake during a battle.
explanation.definitionFit: Waterloo was the 1815 battle where Napoleon was finally defeated.

clue.text: Total failure with a job the police go out on

parts.note: W is the abbreviation for with
taken as written

parts.words: job the police go out on
parts.note: police slang for an emergency call that sends officers out

explanation.surface: A disastrous police operation from start to finish.
explanation.walkthrough: In British police and fire-service slang a shout is a call-out to an incident.
explanation.definitionFit: A washout is an event that fails completely, like a sports match ruined and abandoned because of rain.

clue.text: Ice bank

definitions.meaning: first meaning: coolness of manner, a cold aloofness
second meaning: a stock held back for later use

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a frozen riverbank or a bank of ice; the two words are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: Reserve is emotional restraint or frostiness, and it is also a stockpile kept back, like money held in a bank.

clue.text: Dishes stuffed with bits of allspice chef makes less hot

indicators.note: something stuffed has a filling put inside it

parts.note: plates are dishes

indicators.note: bits of the next two words means just a small piece of each, their opening letters

parts.note: the opening letters of allspice and chef

explanation.surface: A cook cooling down a fiery recipe by filling plates with allspice.
explanation.walkthrough: Less hot looks like milder food; it means less hot-tempered.
explanation.definitionFit: To placate someone is to calm their anger, making a hot-tempered person cooler.

clue.text: The Queen's one to load load in spin dryer

indicators.note: in a spin means whirling round, so the letters are tumbled into a new order

parts.note: the royal we is how a monarch says one or I
a load is a lot

explanation.surface: The Queen herself loading washing into a spin dryer.
explanation.walkthrough: The printed clue repeats load, apparently a typo; only one load is used. 'Spin dryer' looks like one appliance, but spin signals the jumble and dryer is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A towel is the cloth you use to dry yourself, so it is literally something that dries.

clue.text: Great meal, but no starter at Queen's commemorative event

indicators.note: with no starter the first letter of the meal is left off

parts.note: a feast is a great meal
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the Queen

explanation.surface: A grand dinner held without a first course at a royal celebration.
explanation.walkthrough: Starter looks like the first course; it is the first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Easter is the Christian festival that commemorates the resurrection of Jesus.

clue.text: Senior metalworker must lose weight

indicators.note: the tradesman has to give something up, so a letter is removed

parts.note: a welder joins metal
W is the abbreviation for weight

explanation.surface: An older metalworker being told to slim down.
explanation.definitionFit: An elder is a person who is older or of higher rank, such as a senior member of a church or tribe.

clue.text: Criminal coward rues lot, being yellow as old grass

indicators.note: something criminal is crooked or bent, so the letters are twisted out of order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A lawbreaking coward regrets his fate, being yellow in both senses.
explanation.walkthrough: Yellow suggests cowardly, matching coward; here it is a colour.
explanation.definitionFit: Straw is dried old grass stalks, pale yellow in colour, so straw-coloured describes that shade.

clue.text: Was undecided, so I called up to gain input ultimately

indicators.note: to gain something is to take it in, so the jumble encloses a letter
up here means disturbed or out of order, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: ultimately means at the very end, so only the final letter is kept

parts.note: the final letter of input

explanation.surface: Someone dithered, so they phoned a friend for advice.
explanation.definitionFit: To oscillate is to swing back and forth, and figuratively to waver between opinions without deciding.

clue.text: Make ready, as con leaving back of jail

indicators.note: leaving means departing, so that letter goes out of the word

parts.note: to con a text is to study or memorise it

indicators.note: the back of a word is its final letter

parts.note: the final letter of jail

explanation.surface: A convict leaving prison, getting set for life outside.
explanation.walkthrough: Ready is British slang for cash, as in 'the readies'; con looks like a convict but means study.
explanation.definitionFit: To earn is to make money, and ready is slang for money, so the phrase means gaining cash.
